title: Scoped telemetry tracelet generator and bulk PII sanitizer for on-call sharing
author: Sofia Patel
release_notes: Adds a compact tracelet generator and a configurable bulk sanitizer to allow on-call engineers to share minimal, privacy-safe telemetry snippets with external teams and support. Opt-in via incident labels; RBAC-aware. Improves triage speed while reducing PII exposure.
description:
Summary: This PR introduces a small, portable telemetry snapshot format called a 'tracelet' and a bulk sanitizer pipeline to scrub PII and high-entropy secrets before attachments are uploaded or shared. Motivation: on-call engineers frequently paste long traces or logs into tickets or Slack which contain sensitive material; we need a first-class, low-friction way to extract the minimum diagnostic context and safely share it with support partners and security. 

What changed: checklist: - [x] implement tracelet generator (tracelet.py) with time-bounded spans and metric rollups - [x] add bulk sanitizer (sanitizers/bulk_sanitize.py) with regex rules, entropy detection, and allowlist hooks - [x] wire incident-bot attachment pipeline to run sanitizer before external uploads - [x] CLI flag incident-bot collect --tracelet to create portable JSONL artifacts - [x] unit + integration tests + sample dashboard link - [x] docs update and on-call playbook snippet

Commits (high level): - feat(tracelet): add scoped Tracelet class and serializer - feat(sanitize): implement modular rule engine and entropy detector - chore(ci): add integration test matrix for sanitizer rules - fix(test): address flakiness by adding deterministic timestamping - docs: add playbook and examples

Files touched (high level): - incident-bot/handlers/tracelet.py: core generator and sampling policy - incident-bot/cli/collect.py: new --tracelet flag and upload flow - incident-bot/sanitizers/bulk_sanitize.py: rule engine, entropy heuristics, allowlist hooks - incident-bot/tests/test_tracelet.py and test_sanitize.py - docs/oncall/tracelet-sharing.md - manifests/rbac-sample.yaml (opt-in role for external-share)

Design notes: Tracelets are intentionally minimal — 30s max window by default, aggregated latency buckets, stack sample pointers (no full stack dumps), and embedded sample hashes to detect repetition. The sanitizer pipeline runs rule modules in a configurable order: allowlist -> regex scrub -> entropy mask -> context-aware redaction. Customers can add enterprise allowlists via KMS-backed rule bundles.

Privacy & Security: This PR purposely avoids exporting raw request bodies and long-form user identifiers. All sanitizer rules are reversible only for internal teams (via audit logs) and external uploads remove reversible metadata. RBAC gating ensures only roles with 'external-share' can trigger uploads. The manifests/rbac-sample.yaml provides an example role to grant the capability.

Testing & CI: Initial CI run surfaced two flaky tests in the integration matrix; added deterministic timestamps and fixed race in the collector which resolved failures. CI summary: build: pass, unit-tests: pass, integration: pass after rerun, lint: pass, e2e (optional): skipped on fork.

Review thread (abridged): - Ethan Liu (reviewer): "Nice shape. Please add explicit unit tests for entropy thresholds and add a short doc on how to extend allowlists." - Sofia Patel (author): "Added test_sanitize_entropy and docs at docs/oncall/tracelet-sharing.md; updated README with extension points." - Priya Nair (security): "Can we ensure masking is not reversible when artifacts are shared externally? Add a short note in the playbook." - Sofia Patel: "Confirmed: external path strips reversible fields and writes an audit event to a protected log; noted in docs." - Aaron Chen (sre): "Can we make the default window shorter (15s) for high-traffic services?" - Sofia Patel: "Added an env var TRACELET_DEFAULT_WINDOW with fallback to 30s; callers can override per-service." 

Backward compatibility: Non-breaking. Old attachment paths still work; sanitizer is enabled for 'share:external' flows only by default. Admins can enable sanitizer for all attachments via config.

Merge: Squash-merged after approvals from Ethan, Priya, and Aaron. Followups planned: ENG-2042 to add telemetry to Redwood Console UI for tracelet visualization and ENG-1987 for server-side allowlist distribution.

How to use: example: incident-bot collect --incident 12345 --tracelet --sanitize --upload-external=true This produces a tracelet JSONL artifact, runs sanitizer rules, and (if allowed) uploads to the configured external bucket/store with audit logging.

Notes: Kept the implementation small and modular to encourage adoption by other tools (slo-toolkit will consume tracelets in a follow-up). This is intentionally not a full signal export; it's a pragmatic compromise to speed investigations while reducing data exposure.
